content.comment_body: Today I was asked why I develop my projects in Function Block Diagram (FBD) instead of Ladder Diagram (LAD), and I couldn't really give a concrete answer since I have always used FBD. The conversation shifted towards the opinion that LAD might be better.

My feedback applies specifically to using LAD with [product_name] software. Personally, I find programming in LAD with [product_name] to be challenging. 1) Using LAD in [product_name] software tends to be more error-prone. 2) LAD does not offer as many features as FBD within [product_name] software. 3) The LAD interface can be quite confusing in this environment.

analysis.insight_summary: Users indicate a preference for Function Block Diagram (FBD) over Ladder Diagram (LAD) within [product_name] software. LAD is seen as more prone to mistakes, offers fewer features, and is viewed as less user-friendly compared to FBD, resulting in a less efficient programming experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect both LAD and FBD programming environments within [product_name] software to offer similar levels of functionality, usability, and reliability.
